name: High Peaks Elementary (Core Knowledge focus school)
district: Boulder Valley School District (BVSD), Boulder, Colorado
note: What a learner meets at school each month, mapped to taxonomy topics (Marble mt_ ids and local lt_ ids). Pacing is approximate: units are placed by the school's published Core Knowledge curriculum maps and typical unit lengths; the classroom may run a little ahead or behind. See docs/SCHOOL.md for sources and how this file was built. Months: 1 = January … 12 = December; the school year runs August (8) to May (5).

programs.subject: Mathematics
programs.name: Illustrative Mathematics K-5 (Imagine Learning)
programs.note: BVSD elementary core adoption, 2025. Supplemental: IXL. The Colorado Department of Education also provides free access to Zearn Math.

programs.subject: English
programs.name: HMH Into Reading (K-5) with Fundations (K-3) phonics
programs.note: BVSD core literacy adoption (Into Reading 2023, all schools from 2024-25; Fundations 2018). Supplemental: IXL, Lexia Core5. Screening: Amplify mCLASS with DIBELS 8th Edition.

programs.subject: Science
programs.name: FOSS Next Generation (grades 1-5) + Core Knowledge science units
programs.note: BVSD core science adoption, 2022. FOSS grade 2 modules: Pebbles, Sand, and Silt; Solids and Liquids; Insects and Plants. High Peaks teaches them alongside its Core Knowledge science map.

programs.subject: History
programs.name: Core Knowledge Sequence (history, geography, civics)
programs.note: High Peaks is a BVSD focus school: Core Knowledge content is taught alongside the district curriculum and the Colorado Academic Standards (social studies 2022).

programs.subject: Personal & Social Development
programs.name: Second Step
programs.note: Social-emotional learning lessons; daily class 'campfire' community time.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Adding, subtracting, and working with data
units.note: Fluency within 20, picture and bar graphs, diagrams to compare.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Adding and subtracting within 100
units.note: Decomposing to subtract; story problems with unknowns in all positions.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Measuring length
units.note: Centimeters and meters, then inches and feet; line plots.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Addition and subtraction on the number line
units.note: The structure of the number line; adding and subtracting on it.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Numbers to 1,000
units.note: Hundreds, tens and ones; compare and order within 1,000; skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Geometry, time, and money
units.note: Shape attributes; halves, thirds and fourths; time to five minutes; dollars and cents.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Adding and subtracting within 1,000
units.note: Place-value strategies with and without composing or decomposing tens and hundreds.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Equal groups
units.note: Odd and even; rectangular arrays as a foundation for multiplication.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Putting it all together
units.note: Review of fluency within 20, measurement and numbers to 1,000; writing and solving story problems.

units.subject: English
units.title: Phonics and spelling (Fundations Level 2)
units.note: Vowel teams, two-syllable words, prefixes and suffixes, reading with accuracy and expression.

units.subject: English
units.title: Grammar, punctuation and writing craft
units.program: Into Reading writing workshop, all year
units.note: Capitals and end marks, irregular plurals and past tenses, adjectives vs adverbs, expanding sentences, revising.

units.subject: English
units.title: Writing genres: narrative, informational, opinion, poetry, letters
units.program: Into Reading writing workshop, all year
units.note: The genres the 2nd grade team lists: narrative, informational text, opinion, poetry, correspondence.

units.subject: English
units.title: Vocabulary and word meaning
units.note: Shades of meaning, word parts as clues, using new words.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 1: Be a Super Citizen
units.note: Stories about being a good citizen; central message and story structure. Pairs with civics.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 2: Look Around and Explore
units.note: Nonfiction text features; exploring the world and asking questions like a scientist.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 3: Meet in the Middle
units.note: Solving problems together; main topic and key details; how characters respond to challenges.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 4: Once Upon a Time
units.note: Fairy tales and folktales; comparing versions of the same story; lessons and morals.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 5: Lead the Way
units.note: Leaders and leadership; pictures and text working together. Pairs with civics.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 6: Weather Wise
units.note: Weather texts; sensory language; cloud types, weather instruments and forecasting.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 7: Everyone Has a Story
units.note: Personal and family stories; narrative writing and telling a story aloud. Pairs with immigration.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 8: Time to Grow
units.note: Plants and growing; informational writing. Pairs with the plants science unit.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 9: Home Sweet Habitat
units.note: Habitats; shared research projects. Pairs with the insects and plants science unit.

units.subject: English
units.title: Module 10: Many Cultures, One World
units.note: Stories from many cultures; morals in fables and folktales.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Landforms and changing land
units.program: Core Knowledge: Landforms; FOSS: Pebbles, Sand, and Silt
units.note: Shapes of land and water, fast and slow Earth changes, wind and water shaping the land, rocks and soil.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Magnets and electricity
units.note: Magnetic materials and poles, attract and repel, Earth as a magnet and compasses; simple circuits and switches.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Solids, liquids and states of matter
units.program: Core Knowledge: States of Matter; FOSS: Solids and Liquids
units.note: Classifying materials by properties, choosing materials for a purpose, taking apart and rebuilding, heating and cooling changes.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Science biographies
units.note: Leeuwenhoek, Elijah McCoy, Florence Nightingale, Daniel Hale Williams; asking questions and observing with tools.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Insects and plants
units.program: Core Knowledge: Insects; FOSS: Insects and Plants
units.note: Insect body plan and life cycles, social insects, pollination and seed dispersal, what plants need, diversity of life in habitats. Ends with the Insect Museum.

units.subject: Science
units.title: The digestive system and healthy eating
units.note: Cells, tissues and organs; the digestive journey; a balanced diet. Ends with the crawl-through digestive system.

units.subject: History
units.title: Maps and globes
units.note: Map keys, compass rose, continents and oceans, equator and hemispheres, Colorado and the United States' neighbors.

units.subject: History
units.title: The Constitution and the War of 1812
units.program: Core Knowledge: American Government; The War of 1812
units.note: We the People, James Madison, what government does, Dolley Madison and the White House, Fort McHenry and the anthem.

units.subject: History
units.title: Economics and personal finance
units.program: Core Knowledge map: Economics, Personal Finance
units.note: Goods and services, needs and wants, scarcity, earning, saving, budgeting, making change.

units.subject: History
units.title: Immigration and citizenship
units.note: Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty, why people come to America, rights and responsibilities. Ends with the Ellis Island / Ancestor Dolls event.

units.subject: History
units.title: Civil rights and changemakers
units.program: Core Knowledge: Fighting for a Cause
units.note: Susan B. Anthony, Eleanor Roosevelt, Mary McLeod Bethune, Jackie Robinson, Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King Jr., Cesar Chavez; fairness and equality.

units.subject: History
units.title: Ancient Greece
units.program: Core Knowledge: The Ancient Greek Civilization
units.note: Athens and Sparta, democracy, Marathon and Thermopylae, the Olympics, gods and the Parthenon, Greek theatre. Ends with the Ancient Greek plays.

units.subject: Personal & Social Development
units.title: Growth mindset and goal-setting
units.note: Mistakes help you learn; breaking goals into steps; positive self-talk.

units.subject: Personal & Social Development
units.title: Emotion management
units.note: Naming feelings, mild to strong emotions, calming strategies.

units.subject: Personal & Social Development
units.title: Empathy and kindness
units.note: Seeing another point of view; different lives; being an upstander.

units.subject: Personal & Social Development
units.title: Problem-solving
units.note: Stop, think, then choose; resolving disagreements with friends; working well in a group.
